title: What makes high-volume assembly lines hard to run
why: Only bottleneck work raises line capacity; sampled quality checks let some defects slip through; labor must be balanced and workers trained.

title: Using RSS feeds for HN, security and commits
why: Feed readers can replace social networks, and hnrss provides feeds for replies, Ask HN, Show HN; CVE and commit feeds track security updates.

title: DigitalOcean's public response to UDP traffic incident
why: Company timeline of abuse-monitoring tickets and a customer's database dump script; mostly a dispute narrative with little general lesson.

title: Opinion on indie studios versus Hollywood
why: Argues for a Corman-style studio with many low-risk projects; opinion about film economics without concrete evidence.

title: Opinion on bitcoin's built-in economic assumptions
why: Argues that fixed monetary rules remove democratic say over economic behavior; a values argument rather than technical explanation.

title: Why Microsoft shifted Windows testing to telemetry
why: After tester layoffs, quality moved to developers, beta users and telemetry; crash dumps help debug crashes that testing misses.

title: Why submenus open after a delay
why: Apple's 1995 guidelines explain that submenu delay stops accidental opening when the pointer crosses menu items on the way to a target.

title: Why China's maps use obfuscated GCJ-02 coordinates
why: China requires GCJ-02 coordinates, so applying them to WGS-84 maps offsets locations by 50-500m; open conversion libraries exist.

title: Why early 4K monitors were hard to drive
why: HDMI and DisplayPort versions lacked 4K60 support, so monitors used two tiled streams, which OS drivers and X11 handled poorly.

title: Opinion that manned fighter jets are obsolete
why: Unqualified opinion that drones will outperform crewed fighters by 2040; speculative with no technical explanation of the tradeoffs.

title: Why people keep old iPhones longer
why: Repair-shop experience: monthly phone plans make upgrades costly to see, and cheap, fast screen repairs extend device life.

title: Personal story about discovering APL
why: Anecdote about a 1970s college computer lab and APL's terseness; the programming lesson is thin and mostly autobiographical.

title: What made early Agile teams work well
why: Estimates stayed estimates, standups were team-only, and demos were honest; management metrics and self-promotion later eroded these practices.

title: Critique of talent going to consumer apps
why: Argues elite engineers are wasted on airport pickup apps; a values opinion about startup priorities rather than technical knowledge.

title: Core UI and UX basics engineers should learn
why: Visual hierarchy, basic typography, UX thinking and color semantics matter most; Material Design docs explain why interfaces are built this way.

title: Leaderboard of em dash use after ChatGPT
why: Data-driven leaderboard with a SQL query showing em dash frequency before and after ChatGPT; a finding with a caveat, not a lesson.

title: Why Opera's all-in-one design didn't survive
why: Opera bundled mail, feeds, torrents and a fast engine in a tiny package; web technologies made that approach bulky and it lost ground.

title: Opinion that trust is a feature, not a bug
why: Argues blockchain systems treat trust as a bug and assume everyone is a threat; a philosophical opinion without technical substance.

title: Personal take on San Antonio's Tex-Mex food
why: Family cookbook anecdote and restaurant recommendations; cultural memoir with little general learning.

title: Personal preference for suburban living
why: Personal lifestyle reasoning about suburbs versus cities; an opinion without generalizable insight.

title: Personal account of a phone search at a border
why: Anecdote about a Canadian border phone search and a password; intrusive but offers little general technical or policy lesson.

title: Opinion on ex-employees competing with former employers
why: Debate about whether an intern's side project threatens a company; opinion about business ethics with no technical content.

title: Opinion that web bloat matters more than protocols
why: Argues that page bloat, not transport protocols like QUIC, makes the web slow; a useful argument but rhetorical, not explanatory.

title: List of Windows 10 frustrations
why: Complaint list about wake-ups, input device delays and monitor dragging; a rant with troubleshooting details that lack a general lesson.

title: Rebuttal to sympathy for the Google memo
why: Argues against the Google memo and its analogy to Galileo; a political debate comment rather than a technical explanation.

title: How physics confirms results without true replication
why: Big experiments like the LHC replicate through many analyses, internal cross-checks and bias hunting, which differs from repeating an experiment exactly.

title: Hack Club game designer job ad
why: Recruitment ASCII-art post pointing to an SSH job board; no learning content.

title: Personal story of Shazam finding an obscure song
why: Nostalgic story about identifying a Scrubs track; an enjoyable anecdote with no explanation of how the technology works.

title: Matrix project's plan to fix Riot performance
why: Insider roadmap: lazy-loading room members, cross-signing devices and Synapse algorithm changes that cut memory use and sync times.

title: Why Windows Vista earned its bad reputation
why: Vista's problems came from third-party drivers, especially Nvidia, and an overly aggressive SuperFetch that overloaded spinning hard drives after boot.

title: Why Apple network-extension apps are hard to open source
why: Network Extension entitlements tie to a corporate Apple account, so even paying developers cannot build the app freely; signing and Keychain setup are fragile.

title: Why prefilled tax returns work better
why: California's ReadyReturn prefilled government-known data and won high approval, but lobbying by tax software firms and politics stopped it becoming law.

title: Developer's grievance about Apple's app rules
why: Account rejection story and complaints about Apple's policy and motives; firsthand but mostly a complaint without a transferable technical lesson.

title: FISA courts differ from Article III courts
why: FISC is a congressional creation without lifetime tenure or adversarial hearings; Article III lifetime powers do not govern foreign surveillance.

title: Argument for keeping manual car controls
why: Lists everyday maneuvers that need manual control; a product opinion about self-driving design, not a technical explanation.

title: Why cloud providers gain from custom ARM chips
why: Clouds capture chip margin by building their own ARM processors, and portable languages make ARM deployment easy for most developers.

title: Personal experience of the hypnagogic state
why: Firsthand account of observing the drift into sleep imagery; interesting but personal, with no transferable explanation.

title: Why FoldingCoin gives up decentralization
why: Useful proof-of-work tied to external stats needs a trusted central source, so one entity can control coin distribution and could stop it.

title: Use state consumer protection laws to enlarge claims
why: UDAP laws can treble damages and award attorneys' fees, making small consumer claims and arbitration far more valuable against companies.

title: How to give honest software estimates
why: Say when you cannot estimate, offer a short investigation, or timebox bug hunts instead of giving false dates under pressure from managers.

title: How competitive rules get distorted by gaming
why: Any scored game with clear rules invites strategies that win while distorting the activity; Lincoln-Douglas fixes produced similar distortions.

title: Defense of software engineering interviews
why: Argues that tough interviews filter for competent engineers and complaints come from those who fail; an opinion without evidence.

title: Why engagement metrics favor short-term clickbait
why: Experiments picked the best short-term engagement while long-term holdouts went unreviewed, because incentives and promotions rewarded that.

title: Opinion on whether college is worth it
why: Personal case for a degree based on job search and visa experience; opinion without substantive generalizable analysis.

title: Ethics of accepting dubious fund investors
why: Anecdotes about dictator and sovereign-fund money and where to draw ethical lines; opinion rather than technical insight.

title: In mature markets, differentiation is marketing
why: When products converge technically, as cars and bottled water do, brand and positioning drive purchases more than engineering differences.

title: Complaints about working in a shared office
why: Personal list of noise and social awkwardness in coworking spaces; experience with no general lesson beyond annoyance.

title: Why standards-essential patents must be FRAND
why: Standards use patented tech under fair, reasonable, non-discriminatory licensing; the Apple suit targeted abuse of such patents, not the patents themselves.

title: Why law versioning is unlike git
why: Legislative merge conflicts cannot be auto-resolved; parallel branches persist until courts decide, so legal XML standards must model that.

title: Culture war over who gains from automation
why: Discusses automation politics and work ethics with analogies; mostly opinion, with only a passing point about where cleverness lies.

title: Ad-blocker filter rules for YouTube annoyances
why: A uBlock-style filter list hides YouTube cards and branding, and uses scriptlets to neutralize ad-block detection checks.

title: Why origins must check Host headers behind CDNs
why: CDNs cannot verify origin ownership, so origins must check the Host header plus Cloudflare IPs, or use mTLS origin pulls or tunnels.

title: Former Marine's struggle to become a programmer
why: Personal career story about CS courses, transfer denials and GI Bill timing; no technical lesson for the general reader.

title: Argument that side projects are realistic
why: Argues people spend leisure time on TV and hobbies, so side projects are feasible; a persuasive opinion with no concrete method.

title: Personal journey from design patterns to simple code
why: Career arc from patterns to minimalist code; experience-based opinion without concrete technique or a clear mental model.

title: Why Google's services use proprietary protocols
why: Licensed map data and anti-abuse needs justify closed protocols; Google can change them freely when one client team sits beside the server team.

title: Opinion on 'trust the science' rhetoric
why: Argues policy questions are economic, not scientific, and criticizes the phrase; a political opinion without technical explanation.

title: REST and HATEOAS explained through websites
why: Hypermedia as the engine of application state describes how browsing works: links and forms drive each step, so REST fits websites like HN.

title: Speculative analysis of Tesla's cash position
why: Stock-focused argument about cash burn, deposits and production targets; speculative investment commentary rather than verified technical insight.

title: Question on choosing Python 3 for new projects
why: Asks what Python 3 offers over other languages; a discussion question and opinion with no substantive answer.

title: Complaint about HN downvoting unpopular views
why: Personal grievance about self-censorship and downvotes on HN; a community meta-complaint with no technical or factual content.

title: Opinion on Uber's race-to-the-bottom economics
why: Argues ride-hailing margins converge to taxi economics and recurring one-time charges signal problems; persuasive opinion, partly speculative.

title: Advice to a young CTO about work-life balance
why: Personal advice about burnout and social life; well-meant but opinion-driven, not technical knowledge.

title: Parent's objection to four-hour take-home tasks
why: Personal schedule argument against long take-home assignments; a fair critique of hiring but experience-based opinion.

title: Why Bitcoin transaction IDs are not lookup keys
why: Transaction IDs can change through malleability, so withdrawals must be found by scanning the chain for matching parameters, not the ID returned.

title: Practical Haskell performance rules for large data
why: Avoid thunk buildup in loops, use Text and ByteString rather than String, Vector for finite data, and streaming libraries like Pipes for large inputs.

title: Science fiction as humanity's concept simulator
why: Sci-fi runs gedankenexperiments that explore technology, society and physical limits free of political or corporate constraints.

title: Critique of nostalgia and utopian thinking
why: Philosophical argument that criticisms of modern society need an idea of the good; a debate comment without concrete technical content.

title: Practical Li-ion battery charging guidance
why: High state of charge degrades Li-ion cells faster, so keeping charge near 30-80%, and avoiding deep cycles, extends battery life.

title: Personal SQL formatting style
why: Describes lowercase keywords, indentation and line-folding preferences; a style preference rather than a transferable technique.

title: Defense of unpaid interview homework
why: Argues take-home tasks are fair given high tech salaries; an opinion about hiring fairness without substantive technical content.

title: Pitfalls of adopting Elixir in a company
why: Small hiring pool, thinner libraries, weak editor tooling and needing persistence despite 'no Redis' claims make Elixir costly to maintain long term.

title: Managed access points beat consumer routers
why: Consumer routers as access points cause trouble; centrally managed APs share roaming and channel data and need one settings pane.

title: DigitalOcean's statement on droplet scrubbing
why: Company explanation of snapshot-on-destroy and a scrub default mistake; a responsive incident statement with limited general technique.

title: Opinion that one global language would help
why: Argues for replacing thousands of languages with one, and bemoans historical manuscript finds; an opinion without evidence.

title: Skepticism about dumping time zones
why: Questions whether a unified time zone really saves translation costs and mental effort; a skeptical reader's argument, not a learning source.

title: Critique of Posterous reposting copyrighted content
why: Argues a company blog copied a Quora answer without fair use; a copyright and community complaint rather than technical learning.

title: Quoted study on music while programming
why: Partial quote of a Cornell study about music and programming tasks; the comment is an incomplete excerpt without a clear takeaway.

title: Personal story of a quick profitable t-shirt project
why: Anecdote about launching a viral t-shirt in four hours; an entertaining case story without a transferable lesson.

title: 2013 list of tools for web startups
why: Categorized list of testing, tracking, CI, monitoring and planning tools for small web teams; a useful resource list from that era.

title: Opinion on college enrollment trends
why: Argues weak schools should close and students should choose trades; an opinion about higher education economics without evidence.

title: Opinion on Musk's Twitter offer and moderation
why: Commentary on long-form tweets and moderation norms with personal judgment; opinion about social platforms, not substantive technical insight.

title: Personal argument against overprotecting kids
why: Childhood memory and argument that overprotection harms resilience; an opinion piece based on personal experience.

title: Opinion that the world is miraculous
why: Philosophical claim that we should see the world as miraculous and psychedelics might help; spiritual opinion without evidence.

title: Debate on hypocrisy and free speech in complaints
why: Argues a critic who was refunded cannot claim a grievance; a moral debate about speech and business without technical content.

title: Imagined military scenario with Spot robots
why: Speculative fiction about robot dog armies and creepiness of damaged machines; imaginative commentary without substantive technical content.

title: Review of a Goenka vipassana retreat
why: Personal retreat review noting religious chanting despite dogma-free marketing; experience-based, useful as a warning but not a technical lesson.

title: Self-taught engineer asks how to learn CRDTs
why: Confession and request for advice on learning CRDTs without a degree; a question rather than an explanation of the concept.

title: US high-speed rail struggles: infrastructure, not rules
why: Acela's speed limit comes from lacking grade-separated track, not FRA weight rules; the trains can run 155+ mph on suitable track.

title: Claims about Islamic law and slavery
why: Contested historical and religious claims about slavery in Islam and Christianity; a polemical comment with unreliable sourcing.

title: Keep copies of source code and licenses
why: Acquisitions scatter files and knowledge; a developer kept SimCity port contracts and source copies, which later enabled relicensing discussions.

title: Opinion that JavaScript should be abandoned
why: Hostile argument that JavaScript is only used because browsers force it; opinionated rant with some cited links but no real analysis.

title: Why early employee equity needs big exits
why: Pay cuts for startup equity mean a $120k engineer needs a sale worth roughly $10-15M once preferred shares and hours are counted.

title: Plastic bottles embody little energy beyond the oil
why: Each bottle holds about 1200 kJ of oil energy, while molding and transport add only small amounts; the main cost is landfill persistence.

title: How a dead-man switch failed in a train crash
why: A driver's heart attack kept the pedal pressed with his leg, so the dead-man switch never triggered; rail designs need pedal-release checks.

title: Argument that interest rates will stay low
why: Economic argument that central banks, governments and retirees all want low rates; speculative macro opinion rather than verified analysis.

title: Prediction about Firefox moving away from XUL
why: Predicts that HTML Firefox will lose features and that Thunderbird will be cut; speculative opinion with a bet, not evidence.

title: Military view on the Manning disclosures
why: Argues Manning's disclosures were not proper whistleblowing and compares to other cases; a political opinion about a contested case.

title: Speculation about why Amazon builds Echo
why: Argues Echo's value is a home-control position rather than training data; speculative business reasoning without verified facts.

title: Why resume tools should export Word files
why: Argues resume builders should support Word export and criticizes business models; a product opinion with a self-promotional open-source plug.
